summary: Karma Lekshe Tsomo specializes in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi under the 14th Dalai Lama. She taught at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and University of Hawaiʻi (2023).
Karma Lodrö Chökyi Sengge was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (1973) and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Karma Phuntsho works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a D.Phil. from Oxford under Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich, and held posts at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute (1994), CNRS (~2003–2005), and Cambridge (~2003–2005).
Karma Shedrub Chokyi Sengge studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and taught Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned degrees from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and a PhD from the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.
Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School (~1962–1963) and at Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.

Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford (~1983–1986), and the University of Edinburgh (~1987–1988), and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (1999–2008).
Karsé Kongtrul studied under Khakyab Dorje, the 13th Dalai Lama, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, whom he also taught alongside Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahamakut Buddhist University.

Karunesh Shukla is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1991, he served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz specializes in Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, completing her degrees at the University of Bonn. At the University of Bern, she became a full professor (1999) and served as dean (2007–2010).

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian who studied at Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford (M.A. ~1906–1909), and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India (~1936–1937).

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1944).

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as syndic (1881) and vice-chancellor (1892–1893) of the University of Mumbai, and president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1892–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1915–1945) and as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1956–1970).

Kate Crosby is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She has held posts at Cardiff University (attested 2002), the Buddhist Institute (2003), SOAS University of London, and King's College London (attested 2026).
Kate Wharton works in philosophy and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London (attested 2010).
Katharina Sabernig is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017. She has held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed her Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann, and studied under Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.
